html:
On 1 January 1804 at Gonaives, Jean-Jacques Dessalines declared the independence of Haiti, taking the old Taino name for the island. It was the second independent state in the Americas, after the United States.

It was the only nation ever founded by a successful revolt of enslaved people. Slavery was abolished for good, and the first constitutions barred whites from owning land.

Slave holding powers feared the example. France demanded payment before it would recognise Haiti, which led to the independence debt, and the United States withheld recognition until 1862. Haitians honour the date each year by eating joumou squash soup, once forbidden to enslaved people.
